title: Span export sanity gate and latency-aware shedder for Jaeger/Tempo
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During recent traffic spikes we observed long tail export latencies to Tempo and intermittent downstream throttling in SaaS customers. Some spans have malformed tags (large maps, high-cardinality values) that amplify payload size and cause exporter stalls. We need a lightweight verification and shedding layer that maintains SLOs for span export without losing critical traces for high-priority customers.

Scope: implement a pre-export sanity gate and a latency-aware shedder inside the OTLP relay path that: validates span shape, normalizes/drop pathological tags, enforces per-tenant export size limits, and performs graceful shedding based on exporter latency and queue depth. Integrate with existing tracing hooks and metrics so dashboards can show shed rates, per-tenant export latency, and error counts.

Non-goals: full semantic sampling engine (this will be follow-up), deep repair of malformed spans beyond normalization, or changing downstream Tempo/Jaeger schemas.
proposal:
1) Sanity gate: small, fast checks for each batch/span: max tag count, max tag value length, required traceid/spanid format, and JSON size. Reject or normalize (truncate/drop) according to tenant policy.
2) Latency-aware shedder: maintain sliding-window exporter latency percentiles per backend; when p95 exporter latency > threshold or queue depth > threshold, proactively shed low-priority spans based on tenant priority & span attributes (e.g., diagnostics vs. user-facing). Shedding decision is probabilistic with configurable rates to avoid synchronized drops.
3) Buffering policy: tenant-scoped bounded buffer with TTL; when buffer pressure is high, oldest low-priority spans are dropped first.
4) Observability: emit metrics (export_latency_ms, shed_rate, normalized_span_count, rejected_span_count) and tracing hooks to correlate shedding events with application latency dashboards. Add dashboard panels and alerts for unusual shed spikes.
5) Compatibility: work with both OTLP gRPC and HTTP exporters; maintain Jaeger/Tempo envelope compatibility. Provide feature flags for canary rollout.
design_notes: Prefer stateless fast-path for common case: do simple byte-level checks before parsing full span proto to keep CPU overhead low.
Normalization rules stored as tenant policy (KV) and cached locally with TTL 60s to avoid RPC on every span.
Latency signal derived from exporter acks and send duration; use EWMA per backend with configurable half-life for responsiveness.
Shedder uses two axes: tenant priority (reserved buckets for P0/P1 customers) and span importance heuristics (http.server spans > internal debug spans).
Make shedding decisions transparent: include a shed_reason tag on exported metrics/spans when a span is dropped or normalized.
Expose a dry-run mode where decisions are logged/metric'd but not enforced to validate policies against production traffic.

acceptance_criteria: Sanity gate runs per-span with median CPU overhead < 2% at 50k spans/sec (measured in synthetic benchmark).
When exporter p95 latency exceeds threshold, shed_rate increases for low-priority spans and protected tenants see <1% drop of P0 traces.
Metrics for shed_rate and export_latency are available in Prometheus and visible on the Trace Export dashboard.
Dry-run mode validated on 3 internal tenants and anomalies corrected (no customer data loss during dry-run).
Integration test with tempo simulator shows recovery: after spike, exporter latency returns below threshold and shedding rate reduces to 0 within configured cooldown.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overzealous normalization may remove user-critical tags. Mitigation: tenant policy defaults to conservative truncate-not-drop and require PM approval for aggressive drops.
Risk: Shedding correlated across tenants leading to blind spots. Mitigation: staggered probabilistic shedding + per-tenant quotas/reservations.
Risk: Added CPU on relay path. Mitigation: fast-path checks, sampling, and ability to toggle feature flag off quickly.
Risk: Incorrect schema validation causing false rejects. Mitigation: dry-run and integration tests against representative traffic sets.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Deploy code behind feature flag in staging, run synthetic load test and verify Prom metrics (2 days).
Phase 1: Dry-run for internal orgs for 3 days; collect metrics and adjust normalization rules (1 week).
Phase 2: Canary rollout to small set of customers (5) with manual monitoring and rollback plan (1 week).
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to all customers with automation to monitor shed_rate, p95 latency, and error spikes.
